newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy can and must make EMU but time presses - Fossa.
newsitem.headline: Italy can and must make EMU but time presses - Fossa.

text.p: Italy can and must join the single European currency from the start but time is pressing for the government to take action to get the economy into shape, said Giorgio Fossa, Chairman of the Confindustria employers' body.

He told Confindustria's annual meeting that government and parliament must "do everything necessary", including speeding up action on welfare and pension reforms as well as the three-year economic plan (DPEF), 1998 budget and EMU convergence plan.
"If Italy were to remain outside (EMU)...we would find ourselves immediately ranked among countries at risk. We would be subject to the danger of earthquakes on the foreign exchanges," Fossa said.
"All the sacrifices made and results achieved in the last four to five years would be wiped out in a few months. There would be an enormous risk of insolvency in our public debt.

"It would be extremely dangerous to impose economic policy choices on the normal dates of the Italian calendar. We are not facing normal times," Fossa said, criticising the government for delays in presenting the DPEF and urging it not to wait until the last moment before presenting the 1998 draft budget.
"If we were to realise in February 1998 that the budget was no longer sufficient then the markets would express their opinion straightaway and the game would be over," he said.
"But Italy has all the potential to avoid these serious dangers," Fossa said noting that some progress had been made. "Now the work must be completed," he said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
